title: How the Social and Behavioral Sciences Explain Our Reactions to COVID-19 with Jay Van Bavel, PhD

sentences.en: The social and behavioral sciences have much to say about the reasons for many of our behaviors in response to the novel coronavirus.
sentences.zh: 社会和行为科学对于我们应对新型冠状病毒的许多行为原因有很多见解。

sentences.en: How we perceive and navigate threats, whether we believe conspiracy theories, how we demonstrate altruism or not, are all behaviors that scientists from
sentences.zh: 我们如何感知和应对威胁，是否相信阴谋论，如何表现出利他主义与否，这些都是科学家们

sentences.en: many disciplines have studied for years.
sentences.zh: 多年来一直在研究的行为。

sentences.en: In late March, several scholars posted a preprint of an article that was developed by pulling together experts from many disciplines to look at what
sentences.zh: 三月下旬，几位学者发布了一篇预印本文章，他们汇集了多个学科的专家，旨在研究

sentences.en: the research tells us about these and other behaviors.
sentences.zh: 研究告诉我们关于这些行为以及其他行为的结论。

sentences.en: What they concluded may help at least some of us better understand why we're doing what we're doing.
sentences.zh: 他们的结论或许能帮助我们中至少一部分人更好地理解我们为何会有这些行为。

sentences.en: And if we're attentive and intentional, these insights might actually help us act in ways that will help flatten the COVID-19 curve.
sentences.zh: 如果我们保持关注并有意识地行动，这些见解实际上可能有助于我们采取行动，从而帮助拉平新冠疫情的曲线。

sentences.en: Welcome to Speaking of Psychology, the flagship podcast of the American Psychological
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听《心理学谈话》，这是美国心理学

sentences.en: Association that examines the links between psychological science and everyday life.
sentences.zh: 协会的旗舰播客，旨在探讨心理科学与日常生活之间的联系。

sentences.en: I'm
sentences.zh: 我是

sentences.en: Kim Mills.
sentences.zh: 金·米尔斯。

sentences.en: Our guest today is Dr. Jay Van Bevel, an expert on group identities, moral values, and political beliefs.
sentences.zh: 我们今天的嘉宾是杰伊·范·巴维尔博士，他是群体认同、道德价值观和政治信仰方面的专家。

sentences.en: He is an associate professor of psychology and neuroscience at New York University, where he directs the Social Perception and Evaluation Lab.
sentences.zh: 他是纽约大学心理学和神经科学副教授，并在那里指导社会感知与评估实验室。

sentences.en: His research examines implicit bias, diversity and inclusion, team performance, cooperation, and decision-making.
sentences.zh: 他的研究涉及内隐偏见、多元化与包容性、团队绩效、合作以及决策制定。

sentences.en: Welcome to
sentences.zh: 欢迎来到

sentences.en: Speaking of Psychology, Dr. Van Bevel.
sentences.zh: 《心理学谈话》，范·巴维尔博士。

sentences.en: Hi, it's nice to be here.
sentences.zh: 你好，很高兴来到这里。

sentences.en: Great.
sentences.zh: 太好了。

sentences.en: You recently gathered something like 41 experts to draft a summary of research findings relevant to how best to handle the COVID-19 response.
sentences.zh: 您最近召集了大约 41 位专家，起草了一份关于如何最好地应对新冠疫情的研究结果摘要。

sentences.en: And you published this article that united psychologists, economists, sociologists, and others for a review of research on fake news and
sentences.zh: 你们发表了这篇文章，联合了心理学家、经济学家、社会学家和其他学者，对有关假新闻和

sentences.en: conspiracy theories, leadership, threat perception, and other issues that are all at play in the ongoing public health crisis.
sentences.zh: 阴谋论、领导力、威胁感知以及在当前公共卫生危机中发挥作用的其他问题进行了综述。

sentences.en: Can you tell our listeners some of what you all concluded?
sentences.zh: 您能告诉我们的听众你们得出的一些结论吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So basically what we tried to do is pull together what we thought was the best evidence and research in many fields that might be relevant to COVID-19.
sentences.zh: 基本上，我们试图做的是汇集我们认为在许多领域中与新冠疫情相关的最佳证据和研究。

sentences.en: So obviously COVID-19 is new and we're doing tons of research on it right now, but there isn't a lot of published research.
sentences.zh: 显然，新冠疫情是新的，我们现在正在对其进行大量研究，但已发表的研究并不多。

sentences.en: So we drew as much as we could from prior pandemics, public health messages, and other topics that we thought were relevant.
sentences.zh: 因此，我们尽可能多地借鉴了以往的流行病、公共卫生信息以及我们认为相关的其他主题。

sentences.en: And many of the ideas that we came up with were around things like, you know, getting people
sentences.zh: 我们提出的大多数想法都围绕着，你知道，让人们

sentences.en: to manage the threats, encouraging social connection during a period of isolation and distancing, also work on how to deal with misinformation.
sentences.zh: 去管理威胁，在隔离和保持社交距离期间鼓励社会联系，以及如何处理错误信息。

sentences.en: So you mentioned conspiracy theories, as well as fake news, and how to give leaders and members of the public insights about what ways they
sentences.zh: 所以你提到了阴谋论以及假新闻，以及如何让领导者和公众了解他们

sentences.en: can engage in effective persuasion and communication.
sentences.zh: 可以采取哪些方式进行有效的说服和沟通。

sentences.en: And so we tried to pull all that together.
sentences.zh: 所以我们试图把所有这些整合在一起。

sentences.en: And again, our paper is really a consensus across sciences.
sentences.zh: 再次强调，我们的论文确实是跨学科的共识。

sentences.en: It's not just psychological science, but collaboration between many people in many different disciplines to figure out what we
sentences.zh: 这不仅仅是心理科学，而是许多不同学科的许多人之间的合作，以找出我们在

sentences.en: kind of tended to agree on across all of these different disciplines.
sentences.zh: 所有这些不同学科中倾向于达成一致的观点。

sentences.en: One concept that your paper discusses is optimism bias, the notion that bad things are more likely to happen to other people, not to me.
sentences.zh: 您的论文讨论的一个概念是乐观偏见，即认为坏事更有可能发生在别人身上，而不是自己身上。

sentences.en: How can leaders use communication strategies that strike a balance between breaking through this optimism bias without inducing excessive feelings of anxiety and dread?
sentences.zh: 领导者如何使用既能打破这种乐观偏见，又不会引起过度焦虑和恐惧的沟通策略？

sentences.en: Yeah, dealing with optimism bias is challenging.
sentences.zh: 是的，处理乐观偏见很有挑战性。

sentences.en: And optimism bias in this context essentially takes the form of understanding the risks.
sentences.zh: 在这种背景下，乐观偏见本质上表现为对风险的理解。

sentences.en: Maybe you're watching the news or TV, and you realize there's a very real risk of this virus spreading and people maybe even in your community getting the disease.
sentences.zh: 也许你在看新闻或电视，意识到这种病毒传播以及人们甚至在你所在的社区感染这种疾病的风险是非常真实的。

sentences.en: But you might think optimistically that you're not going to get it.
sentences.zh: 但你可能会乐观地认为自己不会感染。

sentences.en: And if you have that thought that you are less likely to get it than the next person, then you might be more inclined to take risks.
sentences.zh: 如果你认为自己比别人更不容易感染，那么你可能更倾向于冒险。

sentences.en: And that might mean going out more, traveling more, maybe being less inclined to do things like wear a mask.
sentences.zh: 这可能意味着更多地外出、更多地旅行，或者不太愿意做戴口罩之类的事情。

sentences.en: And naturally, if you do those things, that puts you at risk.
sentences.zh: 自然地，如果你那样做，就会让自己处于危险之中。

sentences.en: And so one of the things that we're trying to communicate to people is that even if they're effective at communicating the risks, they nevertheless have to change the behavior
sentences.zh: 所以我们试图向人们传达的一件事是，即使他们能有效地传达风险，他们仍然必须改变

sentences.en: of specific individuals.
sentences.zh: 特定个人的行为。

sentences.en: And one way, one section we have is on social norMs. And it turns out that social norms in many different areas tend to be an effective way of changing behaviors, even if people
sentences.zh: 我们有一个章节是关于社会规范的。事实证明，在许多不同领域，社会规范往往是改变行为的有效方式，即使人们

sentences.en: don't necessarily change their own attitudes or perceptions.
sentences.zh: 不一定改变他们自己的态度或看法。

sentences.en: So if they see other people wearing masks, and you can kind of find good role models and ways of communicating that as the new norm,
sentences.zh: 所以如果他们看到别人戴口罩，并且你能找到好的榜样，并以某种方式将其作为新的规范进行传播，

sentences.en: then people might do it even if they don't necessarily think that they're at a particular high risk.
sentences.zh: 那么人们即使不认为自己处于特别高的风险中，也可能会这样做。

sentences.en: They'll do it because it's normative, because when they walk in a restaurant, everybody
sentences.zh: 他们会这样做是因为这是规范，因为当他们走进餐厅时，每个人

sentences.en: else is wearing masks, or because when they walk down a running trail, everybody else is wearing masks.
sentences.zh: 都在戴口罩，或者因为当他们走在跑步道上时，每个人都在戴口罩。

sentences.en: And so that's essentially what we try to do is basically provide insights from the literature
sentences.zh: 所以这基本上就是我们试图做的，即提供文献中的见解，

sentences.en: that might be effective ways to move the needle on some of these public health behaviors, especially despite the types of psychological shortcuts and heuristics people often make.
sentences.zh: 这些见解可能是改变这些公共卫生行为的有效方式，特别是考虑到人们经常使用的心理捷径和启发式方法。

sentences.en: I have one family member who says it's okay to go out where she lives, which is on an island in
sentences.zh: 我有一位家庭成员说，在她住的地方，也就是佛罗里达州的一个岛上，出门是可以的，

sentences.en: Florida, because no one on that island has died from COVID yet.
sentences.zh: 因为那个岛上还没有人死于新冠。

sentences.en: But she's over 80 and has lung ailments, and thus she's part of the highest risk cohort.
sentences.zh: 但她已经 80 多岁了，患有肺部疾病，因此她属于最高风险群体。

sentences.en: How do we get through to people like that who, it seems, just don't grasp the mathematical probability of getting ill?
sentences.zh: 我们如何才能说服像她这样似乎根本无法理解患病数学概率的人？

sentences.en: Yeah, so one thing we might need to do is find ways of communicating the norm to her.
sentences.zh: 是的，所以我们需要做的一件事是找到向她传达规范的方法。

sentences.en: So if the people in your friend's community are wearing masks, or if your friend is a member of a local
sentences.zh: 如果你的朋友所在的社区里的人都在戴口罩，或者如果你的朋友是当地

sentences.en: church or parish or synagogue or mosque, if the religious leaders in that community wear masks and model it, that might be something that nudges your friend to do it.
sentences.zh: 教堂、教区、犹太教堂或清真寺的成员，如果该社区的宗教领袖戴上口罩并做出表率，这可能会促使你的朋友也这样做。

sentences.en: Even if they don't think that they're at unique risk, they might think they're still relatively safe.
sentences.zh: 即使他们不认为自己处于独特的风险中，他们可能仍然认为自己相对安全。

sentences.en: But if everybody else is doing it, and they're going to get, you know, eyes rolled at them or people making comments to them when
sentences.zh: 但如果其他人都在这样做，而且当他们外出时，别人会向他们翻白眼或对他们发表评论，

sentences.en: they're out, they might be more like to wear a mask, even if they don't think it's particularly risky in their island or neighborhood or what have you.
sentences.zh: 他们可能更愿意戴口罩，即使他们认为在他们的岛屿或社区或其他地方并没有特别大的风险。

sentences.en: Yeah, but we're talking about Florida, you know, what's happening down there.
sentences.zh: 是的，但我们谈论的是佛罗里达，你知道，那里正在发生的事情。

sentences.en: I feel like every news story starts with, you know, Florida man or Florida woman and some remarkable story.
sentences.zh: 我觉得每篇新闻报道都以，你知道，佛罗里达男人或佛罗里达女人和一些非凡的故事开头。

sentences.en: But I'm in New York.
sentences.zh: 但我人在纽约。

sentences.en: So I don't think I can talk about, you know, with too much confidence.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为我不能太自信地谈论它。

sentences.en: We've obviously struggled with our own rates.
sentences.zh: 我们显然在自己的感染率上挣扎过。

sentences.en: And I think one of the things that's challenging with this particular virus is people don't have good models of predicting
sentences.zh: 我认为这种特定病毒具有挑战性的一点是，人们没有很好的模型来预测

sentences.en: risk, especially for exponential, you know, spread, because the way it works is that there's only a couple people who might have it in your community.
sentences.zh: 风险，特别是对于指数级的传播，因为它的工作方式是，你的社区里可能只有几个人感染了。

sentences.en: And then a week later, it's grown exponentially.
sentences.zh: 然后一周后，它呈指数级增长。

sentences.en: And it's a huge amount, which is essentially what happened in New York.
sentences.zh: 数量巨大，这基本上就是纽约发生的情况。

sentences.en: I remember colleagues and friends saying, well, New York's not at that big of risk.
sentences.zh: 我记得同事和朋友说，嗯，纽约的风险没那么大。

sentences.en: You know, they could see the data in Italy, they could see some infections around New York.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他们可以看到意大利的数据，他们可以看到纽约周围的一些感染情况。

sentences.en: But there weren't that many deaths in New York at the time.
sentences.zh: 但当时纽约的死亡人数并不多。

sentences.en: And then a week later, it had blown up.
sentences.zh: 然后一周后，它就爆发了。

sentences.en: And by then it was out of control.
sentences.zh: 到那时已经失控了。

sentences.en: And we've now got it mostly under control.
sentences.zh: 我们现在已经基本控制住了。

sentences.en: But it's, you know, we're the world's hotspot.
sentences.zh: 但你知道，我们是世界的热点地区。

sentences.en: And it was a week before it blew up that I had really smart people around me saying it's not going to be that big of an issue in New York.
sentences.zh: 就在它爆发前一周，我周围非常聪明的人还说，在纽约这不会成为什么大问题。

sentences.en: So that's unfortunately, one of the psychological challenges of dealing with infectious diseases like this.
sentences.zh: 所以不幸的是，这是应对此类传染病的心理挑战之一。

sentences.en: A lot of people tend to expect that there'll be a real panic during a disaster like this.
sentences.zh: 很多人倾向于认为在这样的灾难中会发生真正的恐慌。

sentences.en: And it doesn't seem to be happening other than this talk about panic buying, which might not even be a real thing.
sentences.zh: 除了关于恐慌性购买的讨论（这甚至可能不是真实存在的）之外，这种情况似乎并没有发生。

sentences.en: What does the research say about panic during disasters?
sentences.zh: 研究对灾难中的恐慌有什么说法？

sentences.en: Yeah, that's a great question.
sentences.zh: 是的，这是一个很好的问题。

sentences.en: And to be honest, that was one of the most surprising
sentences.zh: 老实说，这是我们论文中包含的最令人惊讶的

sentences.en: literatures that we included in our paper.
sentences.zh: 文献之一。

sentences.en: So there's research by John Drury and Steve
sentences.zh: 约翰·德鲁里和史蒂夫·赖彻等人有研究，

sentences.en: Reicher and others who has explored large groups and when they engage in things like panic versus not.
sentences.zh: 他们探索了大型群体以及他们何时参与恐慌与否。

sentences.en: And they find that the notion of panic is actually vastly overblown.
sentences.zh: 他们发现恐慌的概念实际上被大大夸大了。

sentences.en: So if you watch
sentences.zh: 所以如果你看

sentences.en: Hollywood movies about outbreaks and pandemics, they often show images of rioting and panic.
sentences.zh: 关于疫情和流行病的好莱坞电影，它们经常展示骚乱和恐慌的画面。

sentences.en: That's kind of the images that the media in the United States started to show during the early stages of the coronavirus when they showed images of empty shelves and people.
sentences.zh: 这就是美国媒体在冠状病毒早期阶段开始展示的画面，当时他们展示了空货架和人们的画面。

sentences.en: There might be two women fighting over the last rolls of toilet paper at a supermarket.
sentences.zh: 超市里可能有两名妇女在争抢最后几卷卫生纸。

sentences.en: And surely there were some things that were scarce for a period of time.
sentences.zh: 当然，确实有一些东西在一段时间内很短缺。

sentences.en: But the whole notion of panic, again, I'll just say, I live in Manhattan and you haven't seen almost any of that.
sentences.zh: 但关于恐慌的整个概念，我再说一遍，我住在曼哈顿，你几乎没见过这些。

sentences.en: In fact, you haven't seen almost any of it anywhere in the United States or around the world.
sentences.zh: 事实上，你在美国或世界各地的任何地方几乎都没见过这种情况。

sentences.en: It's been very rare.
sentences.zh: 这非常罕见。

sentences.en: And so their research really suggests that when you keep people dealing in these situations, they often come together and have a remarkable amount of collective resilience.
sentences.zh: 所以他们的研究确实表明，当人们在这些情况下保持互动时，他们往往会团结起来，并表现出惊人的集体韧性。

sentences.en: And the notion of panic is, you know, mostly wrong scientifically and certainly vastly oversold.
sentences.zh: 而恐慌的概念，你知道，在科学上大多是错误的，而且肯定被大大夸大了。

sentences.en: So that's one of the things where there's kind of a counterintuitive finding from the science that kind of goes against our intuitions and certainly
sentences.zh: 所以这是科学中一种反直觉的发现，它违背了我们的直觉，当然也违背了

sentences.en: what we expect from watching movies about similar situations.
sentences.zh: 我们从观看关于类似情况的电影中所预期的那样。

sentences.en: What have you observed about how social networks are spreading helpful and harmful information?
sentences.zh: 关于社交网络如何传播有益和有害信息，您观察到了什么？

sentences.en: And are they tending more one way than the other?
sentences.zh: 它们是更倾向于哪一方面？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So I do research myself on social networks and how information spreads online.
sentences.zh: 我自己也研究社交网络以及信息如何在网上传播。

sentences.en: And obviously, this is a big issue in a pandemic, right?
sentences.zh: 显然，这是大流行中的一个大问题，对吧？

sentences.en: Because this is where epidemiologists study the structure of social networks and how viruses spread.
sentences.zh: 因为这就是流行病学家研究社交网络结构以及病毒如何传播的地方。

sentences.en: But there's been a lot of research in the last decade or so looking at how information spreads and using basically those classic epidemiological models
sentences.zh: 但在过去十年左右的时间里，有很多研究观察信息是如何传播的，并基本上使用那些经典的流行病学模型

sentences.en: to understand things like how messages go viral.
sentences.zh: 来理解诸如消息如何病毒式传播之类的事情。

sentences.en: Now, a lot of that work, especially in the last few years, has started to look at things like fake news, misinformation, conspiracy theories.
sentences.zh: 现在，很多这样的工作，特别是在过去几年里，已经开始关注假新闻、错误信息、阴谋论等问题。

sentences.en: And my lab studies those topics as well.
sentences.zh: 我的实验室也研究这些主题。

sentences.en: What we find is that, first of all, most people are not conspiracy theorists.
sentences.zh: 我们发现，首先，大多数人不是阴谋论者。

sentences.en: So when I'm going to talk about things like conspiracy theories, just understand these people are in the minority.
sentences.zh: 所以当我谈论阴谋论之类的事情时，请理解这些人是少数。

sentences.en: But what you should also understand is that when these messages that they have do go viral, millions of people can watch them now because of social media.
sentences.zh: 但你也应该明白，当他们拥有的这些信息确实病毒式传播时，由于社交媒体，现在有数百万人可以看到它们。

sentences.en: So there was a recent video that went viral.
sentences.zh: 所以最近有一个视频病毒式传播了。

sentences.en: I believe it was called The Plandemic.
sentences.zh: 我相信它叫《大流行》（Plandemic）。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And it was this conspiracy theory video on
sentences.zh: 这是一个关于

sentences.en: YouTube and it was watched millions and millions of times within a few days.
sentences.zh: YouTube 的阴谋论视频，在几天内被观看了数百万次。

sentences.en: And it was, again, just a very twisted conspiracy theory without much evidence behind it.
sentences.zh: 而且，它再次只是一个非常扭曲的阴谋论，背后没有太多证据。

sentences.en: And it only takes a couple people spreading those for it to get to millions of eyes in a way that just would have been impossible, you know,
sentences.zh: 只需要几个人传播这些信息，它就能进入数百万人的视野，这在你知道的 20 或 30 年前，

sentences.en: 20 or 30 years ago for a conspiracy theorist to spread information.
sentences.zh: 对于阴谋论者来说是不可能传播信息的。

sentences.en: And so social media allows people to leverage social networks and weaponize misinformation.
sentences.zh: 因此，社交媒体允许人们利用社交网络并将错误信息武器化。

sentences.en: There was an article in The New York Times a couple weeks ago about a conspiracy theory that coronavirus was being spread by 5G wireless towers.
sentences.zh: 几周前《纽约时报》有一篇文章，关于冠状病毒是通过 5G 无线塔传播的阴谋论。

sentences.en: And there were over 100 attacks on towers or people who worked for the telecommunications companies.
sentences.zh: 并且发生了 100 多起针对信号塔或电信公司员工的袭击事件。

sentences.en: And so those are real behaviors.
sentences.zh: 所以这些是真实的行为。

sentences.en: They're putting people at danger.
sentences.zh: 它们使人们处于危险之中。

sentences.en: And not only are they putting those employees and structures at risk, but if they knock down a 5G tower, there goes a lot of people's access to social
sentences.zh: 它们不仅使那些员工和设施处于危险之中，而且如果他们拆毁了 5G 塔，许多人的社会联系渠道也就没了，

sentences.en: connection through, you know, like Zoom meetings and Skyping, their friends and family.
sentences.zh: 比如通过 Zoom 会议和与朋友及家人进行 Skype 通话。

sentences.en: A lot of kids like my kids right now are homeschooling.
sentences.zh: 很多孩子，比如我现在的孩子，都在家上学。

sentences.en: Their internet and Wi-Fi is their capacity to learn.
sentences.zh: 他们的互联网和 Wi-Fi 是他们学习的能力。

sentences.en: And so it's doing that.
sentences.zh: 所以它正在造成这种影响。

sentences.en: And then the third thing I think that is the risk with conspiracy theories is if those people are getting out and they're not taking the medical messaging seriously,
sentences.zh: 我认为阴谋论带来的第三个风险是，如果这些人走出去，并且不认真对待医疗信息，

sentences.en: they're putting themselves at risk.
sentences.zh: 他们就会让自己处于危险之中。

sentences.en: And in a pandemic, that means they're putting everybody at risk in catching the disease.
sentences.zh: 在大流行中，这意味着他们让每个人都处于感染疾病的风险中。

sentences.en: So this is the reason that we're worried about things like conspiracy theories and misinformation.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们担心阴谋论和错误信息之类事情的原因。

sentences.en: It's not just because, you know, those people are, it seems crazy to us, but there's a risk that they spread things throughout the entire community if they're not
sentences.zh: 这不仅仅是因为，你知道，那些人，在我们看来很疯狂，但如果他们不认真对待实际的医疗信息，

sentences.en: taking the actual medical information seriously.
sentences.zh: 他们就有可能在整个社区传播这些东西。

sentences.en: What makes our brains so susceptible to these wacky theories?
sentences.zh: 是什么让我们的大脑如此容易受到这些古怪理论的影响？

sentences.en: That's a good question.
sentences.zh: 这是一个好问题。

sentences.en: So there's lots of different elements of it.
sentences.zh: 所以它有很多不同的要素。

sentences.en: So there's certain types of personality styles that are more or less susceptible to misinformation.
sentences.zh: 所以有某些类型的人格风格更容易或更不容易受到错误信息的影响。

sentences.en: We have a paper in my lab we just submitted yesterday that finds people who kind of have overinflated views of their
sentences.zh: 我的实验室昨天刚提交了一篇论文，发现那些对自己的国家和民族认同有过度膨胀看法的人，

sentences.en: nation and their national identity, they think their country is unique and special, are very likely, it turns out, to believe and share conspiracy theories about COVID-19.
sentences.zh: 他们认为自己的国家是独特和特别的，事实证明，他们非常有可能相信并分享关于新冠疫情的阴谋论。

sentences.en: One of the reasons we think is because the pandemic is threatening to their country.
sentences.zh: 我们认为原因之一是，大流行对他们的国家构成了威胁。

sentences.en: If it spreads, it proves that their country isn't that great or unique as they might think.
sentences.zh: 如果它传播开来，就证明他们的国家并不像他们想象的那样伟大或独特。

sentences.en: And we found this in the United States, but we've also found it in Britain.
sentences.zh: 我们在美国发现了这一点，但在英国也发现了这一点。

sentences.en: So that's one personality style we found that turns out to be a really powerful predictor of conspiracy theory belief.
sentences.zh: 所以这是我们发现的一种人格风格，它被证明是阴谋论信仰的一个非常强大的预测指标。

sentences.en: But there's lots of other work around, you know, when people have needs for control or understanding.
sentences.zh: 但还有很多其他关于，你知道，人们何时有控制或理解需求的研究。

sentences.en: And during a pandemic, you know, they've kind of lost control and they don't fully understand it.
sentences.zh: 在疫情期间，你知道，他们有点失去了控制，而且并没有完全理解它。

sentences.en: So that can heighten conspiracy theories.
sentences.zh: 所以这可能会加剧阴谋论。

sentences.en: You also see many conspiracy theories are xenophobic.
sentences.zh: 你还会发现许多阴谋论都带有仇外心理。

sentences.en: They're often about another nation has created the disease.
sentences.zh: 它们通常是关于某个国家制造了这种疾病。

sentences.en: So there's obviously a conspiracy theory that it was created and weaponized by the Chinese government.
sentences.zh: 所以显然存在一种阴谋论，认为它是中国政府制造并武器化的。

sentences.en: But if you look in other countries, there's conspiracy theories that the United States is behind it.
sentences.zh: 但如果你看看其他国家，也有阴谋论认为美国是幕后黑手。

sentences.en: And so it's a way of a conspiracy theory is often interwoven with group identities and, and, you know, kind of negative malicious beliefs about certain groups as well.
sentences.zh: 所以，阴谋论往往与群体认同交织在一起，也与对某些群体的负面恶意偏见有关。

sentences.en: There's research into this concept of nudges, little things that move people in certain directions.
sentences.zh: 目前有关于“助推”这一概念的研究，即通过一些小事引导人们朝着特定方向行动。

sentences.en: I'm wondering, can you list some examples of nudges you've seen that are influencing people's behaviors and explain how they work?
sentences.zh: 我想知道，你能列举一些你所见过的、正在影响人们行为的“助推”例子，并解释它们是如何运作的吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 可以。

sentences.en: So nudges are basically a soft way of managing behavior.
sentences.zh: “助推”基本上是一种管理行为的柔性方式。

sentences.en: So you have the hard, forceful way of managing behavior, which has been happening in many countries, which is like a lockdown.
sentences.zh: 你可以采取强硬、强制的方式来管理行为，这在许多国家都发生过，比如封城。

sentences.en: I mean, you saw that in Wuhan in China first, where they have an authoritarian government that can just completely lock everybody at home.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你首先在中国武汉看到了这一点，他们有一个威权政府，可以完全把每个人都锁在家里。

sentences.en: But you're seeing it in, in American states where governors are, you know, demanding that all restaurants stay closed and closing all the schools.
sentences.zh: 但你在美国的各个州也能看到这种情况，州长们要求所有餐馆保持关闭，并关闭所有学校。

sentences.en: Um, and so sometimes you need that, you know, to save lives, but it's hard to sustain.
sentences.zh: 嗯，有时候为了挽救生命，你需要这样做，但这很难持续。

sentences.en: Um, so people, uh, might get exhausted or tired or frustrated.
sentences.zh: 嗯，所以人们可能会感到精疲力竭、疲惫或沮丧。

sentences.en: And so you need other ways of encouraging them to engage in the right behaviors to promote public health, um, for a long period of time.
sentences.zh: 因此，你需要其他方式来鼓励他们长期采取正确的行为，以促进公共卫生。

sentences.en: I mean, in New York, it's been, I believe two months or more since, uh, you know, I was told that my university was closing and my kids' schools were closing.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，在纽约，我相信已经有两个月或更长时间了，当时我被告知我的大学要关闭，我孩子的学校也要关闭。

sentences.en: So what can you do to encourage people like me to continue doing the things that promote my safety and the safety of people in my community?
sentences.zh: 那么，你能做些什么来鼓励像我这样的人继续做那些能促进我自身安全以及社区中他人安全的事情呢？

sentences.en: And so nudges are ways of framing issues and decisions that lead to the right behavior.
sentences.zh: “助推”就是通过构建问题和决策的方式，引导人们做出正确的行为。

sentences.en: And this is also one of the places where social norms come in.
sentences.zh: 这也是社会规范发挥作用的地方之一。

sentences.en: So I was just watching our governor, Andrew Cuomo's press briefing, uh, about an hour ago,
sentences.zh: 我大约一小时前刚看了我们州长安德鲁·科莫的简报会，

sentences.en: and his daughter, um, solicited little mini ads to encourage people to wear masks because he's
sentences.zh: 他的女儿制作了一些小广告来鼓励人们戴口罩，因为他意识到，

sentences.en: realizing that's going to be really key to promoting safety in New York and reopening things.
sentences.zh: 这对促进纽约的安全和重启经济至关重要。

sentences.en: And so, um, one of the things in a couple of the ads that were really clever, um, one of the things
sentences.zh: 所以，在几个非常巧妙的广告中，其中一件事，

sentences.en: they did was they had a wide variety of different, uh, New Yorkers putting on the masks for different reasons.
sentences.zh: 他们做的是让各种各样的纽约人出于不同的原因戴上口罩。

sentences.en: So people from all different ethnicities, ages.
sentences.zh: 来自不同种族、不同年龄的人。

sentences.en: And so in those ads, there's a good chance that there's someone that looks like you that's wearing the mask.
sentences.zh: 在这些广告中，很有可能有一个看起来像你的人在戴口罩。

sentences.en: Um, and so I thought that was really good.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我觉得这非常好。

sentences.en: They also had another ad with a guy in front of a building or a subway.
sentences.zh: 他们还制作了另一个广告，主角是一个站在建筑物或地铁前的人。

sentences.en: And he had a shirt that said that guy on it and he wasn't wearing a mask and everyone around it around him was.
sentences.zh: 他穿了一件写着“那家伙”的衬衫，他没有戴口罩，而他周围的所有人都戴着。

sentences.en: And it's, yeah, I like that guy.
sentences.zh: 而且，是的，我喜欢那个家伙。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And he's that guy, the guy who feels like he doesn't have to wear a mask in the subway.
sentences.zh: 他就是“那家伙”，那个觉得自己在地铁里不需要戴口罩的人。

sentences.en: And, um, I saw it and I like you, I just instantly laughed and we all kind of have this notion that we're out in public and there is a guy like that, that just feels like
sentences.zh: 嗯，我看到了，和你一样，我立刻就笑了。我们都有这种观念，当我们身处公共场合时，确实有那样一个人，觉得

sentences.en: they can put everybody else at risk.
sentences.zh: 他们可以把其他所有人都置于危险之中。

sentences.en: And so it was modeling, not only the right behavior, but differentiating it from the wrong behavior and signaling that's wrong, wearing the mask is right.
sentences.zh: 所以这不仅是在示范正确的行为，而且将其与错误的行为区分开来，并发出信号：那是错的，戴口罩才是对的。

sentences.en: And you're going to kind of look like that guy.
sentences.zh: 而且你会看起来像“那家伙”。

sentences.en: And that's how people are going to think of you.
sentences.zh: 人们也会那样看你。

sentences.en: Um, even if they're not saying it when you're out without a mask.
sentences.zh: 嗯，即使当你没戴口罩出门时他们没有说出来。

sentences.en: And so it was like subtle, it didn't require any like shaming or harassment of the person.
sentences.zh: 这很微妙，不需要对那个人进行任何羞辱或骚扰。

sentences.en: It just clearly signaled, don't be that guy.
sentences.zh: 它只是清楚地发出信号：别做“那家伙”。

sentences.en: And so there was lots of like really clever, those were the finalists for this, uh, video messaging competition.
sentences.zh: 所以有很多非常巧妙的广告，那些是这次视频信息竞赛的决赛作品。

sentences.en: And I thought they were, you know, they were funny.
sentences.zh: 我觉得它们很有趣。

sentences.en: Um, they resonated with people that seemed real, but also a lot of the models were, uh, people who looked like all kinds of New Yorkers.
sentences.zh: 嗯，它们引起了人们的共鸣，看起来很真实，而且很多模特都是看起来像各种各样的纽约人。

sentences.en: And so I think that is one of the things I thought it was really clever and well done.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为这是我认为非常巧妙且做得很好的一点。

sentences.en: Um, and so I think like there's lots of subtle ways.
sentences.zh: 嗯，所以我认为有很多微妙的方法。

sentences.en: Another thing that's happening in
sentences.zh: 在纽约发生的另一件事是，

sentences.en: New York is police are going around cause it's getting warm out and they will go to the parks and hand out masks.
sentences.zh: 警察在四处走动，因为天气变暖了，他们会去公园分发口罩。

sentences.en: And so they're, instead of arresting people or coercing people, they're making it as easy for them as possible to wear a mask by giving them free ones.
sentences.zh: 所以，他们不是逮捕或强迫人们，而是通过免费发放口罩，让人们尽可能容易地戴上口罩。

sentences.en: Um, and then the next thing that happens, if those people put on the mask, the police leave, new people come to the park and see that everybody's wearing a mask.
sentences.zh: 嗯，接下来发生的事情是，如果那些人戴上了口罩，警察就会离开，新的人来到公园，看到每个人都戴着口罩。

sentences.en: And that means they'll be more likely to wear a mask just to fit in.
sentences.zh: 这意味着他们为了合群，更有可能戴上口罩。

sentences.en: Um, and so it's a really clever, it kind of does two things by making it easy and natural for people to wear a mask and the police handing them out to make them free.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这真的很巧妙，它通过让人们戴口罩变得容易和自然，并且由警察免费发放，起到了双重作用。

sentences.en: Um, it's more likely to lead them to do it and they don't feel coerced and reactive.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这更有可能引导他们去做，而且他们不会感到被强迫或产生抵触情绪。

sentences.en: And at the same time, they're, they're now sitting in the park with masks on the next wave of people comes and sees, and they get a signal that that's the normative thing to do.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，他们现在戴着口罩坐在公园里，下一波人来了，看到了，他们得到了一个信号，那就是这是规范的做法。

sentences.en: And so I thought that was a really clever, subtle way to nudge the right behavior.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为这是一种非常巧妙、微妙的“助推”正确行为的方式。

sentences.en: And if you do that over a long enough period and now people start wearing masks, it becomes a habit and a norm.
sentences.zh: 如果你在足够长的时间内这样做，人们开始戴口罩，它就会成为一种习惯和规范。

sentences.en: And it's easier to kind of continue that as a, as a way of doing things in the city.
sentences.zh: 而且作为一种在城市中行事的方式，继续这样做会更容易。

sentences.en: And it's so smart because cops are authority figures and here they are, instead of doing
sentences.zh: 这太聪明了，因为警察是权威人物，在这里，他们没有做

sentences.zh: 惩罚性的事情，嗯，你知道，他们以一种让你觉得“我怎么能拒绝呢”的方式敦促你，毕竟是警察给了我口罩。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And it's also, um, I had a former colleague at NYU, uh, Tom Tyler, who did work on procedural justice.
sentences.zh: 而且，嗯，我在纽约大学有一位前同事，汤姆·泰勒，他做过关于程序正义的研究。

sentences.en: And he talked about the need for a place to work with the community and have relationships with the community so that they're seen as legitimate.
sentences.zh: 他谈到了警察需要与社区合作，并与社区建立关系，这样他们才会被视为合法。

sentences.en: Um, and so it also helps with relationships between the community and the police.
sentences.zh: 嗯，所以这也助于改善社区与警察之间的关系。

sentences.en: Um, the police are seen as illegitimate when they are seen as abusing their authority or being coercive or selectively targeting certain groups.
sentences.zh: 嗯，当警察被视为滥用职权、强制执行或有选择性地针对某些群体时，他们会被视为不合法。

sentences.en: Um, and certainly the, the New York police in the past couple of weeks have been accused of only, you know, uh, ticketing or arresting minorities who weren't wearing masks.
sentences.zh: 嗯，当然，纽约警察在过去几周里被指控只对未戴口罩的少数族裔开罚单或进行逮捕。

sentences.en: And so I'm not saying that, uh, the police are perfect, but I think a community policing model where they're working with the
sentences.zh: 所以我并不是说警察是完美的，但我认为一种与公众合作帮助他们的社区警务模式可能是一个更聪明的策略。

sentences.en: public to help them is probably a much smarter strategy.

sentences.en: Visit us at apa.org.

sentences.en: You can also find previous episodes of Speaking of Psychology on our website at speakingofpsychology.org.

sentences.en: And you can subscribe to our podcast on Apple, Stitcher, or wherever you get your podcasts.
